conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode

candidates.name: TripleWitchingDayGapIgnore
candidates.quote: on a triple witching day the SPY's price gets adjusted, and this often results in a gap opening that may be much larger than that on the Emini ... don't be concerned by the gap and just trade the price action as the day unfolds.
candidates.description: Calendar filter: the bar's date is NOT the third Friday of March, June, September or December (triple witching). Intended as a gate on gap-based entries, which Brooks says should be ignored on those days because the opening gap is an ETF price adjustment rather than price action. Identical both sides.

complexity.reason: needs Date decomposition into weekday, month and day-of-month; no price arithmetic

notes: Brooks is describing an ETF artifact, not prescribing a trade; recorded only because 'do not act on the gap that day' is a decidable calendar condition. Low value on futures data.
Only meaningful when paired with a gap-based entry candidate from another chapter.

chapter_summary: A four-page chapter on using ETFs (SPY, SDS, QQQ, QID) and inverse charts as alternative views of the same market. It is almost entirely cross-symbol and chart-configuration advice with no bar-level rules; the only candidate is a low-value triple-witching calendar gate for gap-based entries. Expect nothing here to survive dedup.
